newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's of London 1994 profits top one billion stg.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's of London 1994 profits top one billion stg.

text.p: Lloyd's of London on Friday reported a profit of 1,013 million stg for the 1994 year of account compared with 1,084 the previous year.
The insurance market reports results three years in arrears.
Lloyd's also said it expects a profit of 913 million stg for the 1995 underwriting year of account and 600 million pounds for the 1996 year.
The 1994 results represented a return of 17.8 percent on net written premiums of 5.69 billion stg and was in line with forecasts made last year.
The results include the effects of members' personal expenses including the special contribution to Lloyd's 'Reconstruction and renewal' programme approved by members last year.
Total resources of the Society at December 31 1996 as a percentage of liabilities increased to 184 percent.
The profit in 1994 consists of:
Pure year profit before tax of 1,013 million stg (1993:1,084 million stg).
Profit before personal expenses of 1,667 million stg (1993: 1,720 million stg).
Net release of reserves in respect of prior years of 82 million stg (1993: net strengthening of 859 million stg).
Members' personal expenses of 654 million stg (1993: 636 million stg).
The Personal expenses figure includes 242 million stg contributions to the Central Fund (1993: 183 million stg) and 412 million stg of other expenses (1993:453 million stg).

Lloyd's chairman Sir David Rowland said the result was a consequence of generally good market conditions, the exercise of much-sharpened skills in pricing and the setting of terms by Lloyd's underwriters and a year that contained only a limited incidence of major catastrophes.
On a sectoral basis, Lloyd's pure year result for 1994 was as follows:
Marine 565
Non-marine 837
Aviation 148
Motor 117
Total 1,667
